description: Non-codec video processing domain package for color space conversion, HDR/tone mapping, image signal processing (ISP), and general video pipeline hardware design. Separated from video-codec to maintain clear scope boundaries.

out_of_scope: Codec-specific algorithms (H.264/H.265/AV1 encode/decode) — see video-codec package
Entropy coding, transform, quantization — see video-codec sub-domain experts
scope_definition.codec_alias_note: The video-processing-expert agent in the video-codec package handles codec HW performance analysis (throughput, bandwidth, pipeline). It is NOT part of this package despite the name overlap. This package covers non-codec video processing.

standards.full_name: ITU-R BT.601 — Studio encoding parameters of digital television for standard 4:3 and wide-screen 16:9 aspect ratios
ITU-R BT.709 — Parameter values for the HDTV standards
ITU-R BT.2020 — Parameter values for ultra-high definition television systems
ITU-R BT.2100 — Image parameter values for high dynamic range television

agents.role: Color format conversion — RGB/YUV/Bayer, BT.601/709/2020, chroma subsampling, bit-depth conversion (8/10/12-bit)
Video denoising — spatial NR (bilateral, NLM), temporal NR (3DNR, motion-adaptive), noise modeling, filter HW implementation
Image/video signal processing — HDR tone mapping (PQ/HLG), gamma correction, scaling/resampling, edge enhancement, ISP pipeline architecture

contents.description: V4L2 pixel format overview focused on conversion and storage semantics
Single-planar vs multi-planar storage layout, stride/sizeimage guidance
Common YUV/RGB/Bayer families and conversion implications
Implementation recipes for practical V4L2 format conversion paths
Storage-centric FOURCC comparison and bring-up checklist

knowledge_base.note: Primary baseline is Linux kernel v4.10 media userspace API; where v4.10 pages are sparse/missing (e.g., detailed mplane coverage), supplemental references from v4.8/current docs are listed in each file.

migration_notes.from_video_codec: Non-codec video processing agents are registered here instead of in the video-codec package. Routing in domain-consult/SKILL.md separates codec-performance keywords (-> video-processing-expert in video-codec) from general video keywords (-> vproc agents in this package).
migration_notes.backward_compatibility: The video-processing-expert agent remains in the video-codec package and is NOT moved here. Its name is a historical artifact — it is a codec performance expert, not a general video processing expert.
